channel.title: Kubernetes on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Kubernetes on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.38 is previewing several removals and behavior changes, including kubectl WebSocket opt-out env var removal, kuberc API cleanup, cgroup v1 phaseout, admission webhook filtering for authn/authz review resources, and stricter cgroup driver discovery from container runtimes. Planned upgrades include kuberc and pod-level resources reaching stable, DRA partitionable devices stabilizing, and a new alpha EvictionRequest API.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Pod Sandboxing kata-vm-isolation-v2 runtime class
item.description:
Azure announced a public preview of the kata-vm-isolation-v2 runtime class for pod sandboxing. It is intended to improve isolated pod startup performance and reduce memory overhead compared with classic sandboxed pod flows that boot a new Kata VM per pod.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Agent Sandbox cluster extension
item.description:
Azure is introducing a public preview of an Agent Sandbox cluster extension for Kubernetes. It provides isolated environments for AI agent sessions that run untrusted, model-generated code, reducing the need for teams to build their own sandbox lifecycle and related operational logic.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: DocumentDB enabled by Azure Arc
item.description:
Azure Arc public preview now supports DocumentDB deployment on supported Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters across on-premises, edge, and multicloud environments. It is intended for running MongoDB-compatible document workloads closer to applications.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Pod snapshot cluster extension
item.description:
Azure has a public preview for a pod snapshot cluster extension that helps sandboxed workloads avoid losing in-memory state on restart. It is aimed at reducing reload and warmup costs for AI environments and other applications.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Scheduling the removal of the kube-proxy IPVS backend
item.description:
Kubernetes SIG Network has deprecated the kube-proxy IPVS backend in 1.35 and plans to remove it in 1.40. Users are advised to migrate to nftables on 1.36+ with Linux kernel 5.13+; iptables remains an alternative, with recent performance and scaling improvements.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: From Working Group to SIG Architecture: spotlight on AI Conformance
item.description:
Kubernetes moved AI Conformance from a temporary Working Group into a permanent SIG Architecture subproject after establishing the initial requirements and certification process. The change is meant to keep AI infrastructure requirements vendor-neutral and aligned with Kubernetes architecture as AI workloads become more common.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: aks: Release 2026-10-25
item.description:
AKS release v20261025 adds Kubernetes 1.37 GA/LTS, makes 1.36 the default for new clusters, and ships multiple component and image upgrades. It also introduces several NAP enhancements and previews, plus notable behavior changes around automatic upgrades, Istio, AKS Automatic, etcd encryption, and VMAS-to-VMS migration.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: k8s: Announcing the Workload Conformance Working Group
item.description:
Kubernetes announced a new Workload Conformance Working Group to define a shared, testable standard for workload behavior at runtime. The group will produce a per-minor-version specification, objective tests, and upstream conformance tooling, with initial coverage focused on runtime behavior rather than application logic.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Why Is My Kubernetes Job Still Pending? Tracing Kueue Admission with Headlamp
item.description:
The article introduces the Headlamp Kueue plugin, which helps trace why a Kubernetes Job is still suspended by checking Kueue admission state before looking at Pod scheduling. It walks through a Headlamp-based workflow for inspecting Workloads, LocalQueues, ClusterQueues, ResourceFlavors, and Cohorts, and notes that the 0.1.0-alpha release is read-only.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters
item.description:
Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes will be retired on October 9, 2027. Users should migrate to the Azure Key Vault Secret Store Extension before that date.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: The Shift to cgroup v2 in Kubernetes: What You Need to Know
item.description:
Kubernetes is deprecating cgroup v1 and is moving toward cgroup v2 as the default path: in v1.35, kubelet startup fails by default on cgroup v1 nodes, and kubeadm preflight checks now error on v1.35+ when v1 is detected. The post also summarizes cgroup v2-related behaviors and features in Kubernetes 1.36, including Memory QoS, container-scoped OOM handling, PSI metrics, and in-place pod-level resource updates.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: AKS on bare metal now on Ubuntu
item.description:
Azure has a public preview for running AKS on bare metal using Ubuntu, aimed at on-premises Kubernetes deployments without a virtualization layer. The update highlights support for local control of hardware and software, with a focus on AI workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Scaling Kubernetes Workloads with Node Swap
item.description:
Kubernetes node swap is now GA in v1.34, and this post reports that using fast NVMe Local SSDs for swap can raise pod density for memory-heavy workloads with little latency impact when active working sets remain in RAM.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: aks: Release Notes 2026-09-25
item.description:
AKS release v20260925 adds GA identity bindings, preview support for Ubuntu 26.04 and Windows Server 2022 to 2025 OS SKU migration, and includes multiple behavioral changes, bug fixes, and component updates across Kubernetes versions. It also announces upcoming VMAS cluster auto-migration to VM node pools starting 2026-09-30 and notes that Windows Server 2022 is unsupported on Kubernetes 1.37+.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Flex Nodes for AKS
item.description:
Flex Nodes for AKS is now in public preview. It lets application and platform teams use hybrid and edge infrastructure as connected worker nodes to an AKS control plane in Azure, while keeping a consistent Kubernetes control plane.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Spotlight on SIG Apps
item.description:
SIG Apps is working on workload controller reliability, node lifecycle handling, and new patterns for AI and distributed workloads while preserving backward compatibility. The article highlights current focus areas, the trade-offs in changing core APIs, and a proposed Job API update for Kubernetes 1.38.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Tracking When a PersistentVolumeClaim Was Last Used (Beta)
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 promotes PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime to Beta and enables it by default. PVCs now get an Unused condition in status so you can tell whether any running or pending pod references the claim, and use lastTransitionTime to see when it last became idle.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Hardening Container Storage with Bind Mount Options and EmptyDir Permissions
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 adds alpha support for bind mount options on volume mounts and configurable permission modes for emptyDir volumes. These features let users apply Linux mount flags like noexec, nosuid, and nodev, and set emptyDir modes such as 01777 or 0750 without init-container workarounds.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod-Level Resource Managers graduated to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 graduates Pod-Level Resource Managers to Beta, disabled by default behind the PodLevelResourceManagers feature gate. Kubelet’s Topology Manager, CPU Manager, and Memory Manager can now use pod-level resource declarations for NUMA-aware placement, and the PodResources API reports top-level CPU and memory assignments.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes Changed Block Tracking API - Beta Differences
item.description:
Kubernetes changed block tracking for CSI drivers is now Beta with external-snapshot-metadata v1.0.0. The main Beta change is promotion of SnapshotMetadataService from cbt.storage.k8s.io/v1alpha1 to v1beta1, with no schema change but no served v1alpha1 version.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Memory QoS Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes Memory QoS Beta and turns it on by default, but it does not change runtime behavior unless you explicitly set throttling or reservation fields. The main config change is that memoryThrottlingFactor now defaults to null, so existing clusters will not start writing memory.high unless they already set it.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Native Histograms Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 enables native histogram support for metrics by default and moves the feature to Beta. Components now dual-expose classic buckets and native spans, and users must adjust Prometheus scraping and queries depending on Prometheus version.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Scheduler Preemption for In-Place Pod Resize (Alpha)
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 adds alpha support for scheduler preemption during in-place Pod resize, gated by InPlacePodVerticalScalingSchedulerPreemption. If a running Pod’s resize is Deferred due to lack of node capacity, the scheduler can now preempt lower-priority Pods on the same node so the resize can complete without restarting the Pod.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Introducing Node Lifecycle Conditions
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 reserves five well-known Node lifecycle condition types and adds an alpha feature gate for future built-in behavior, but the gate is disabled by default and no core components act on the conditions yet. The release is meant to provide a shared, Kubernetes-owned signal for drains, maintenance, and graceful shutdown so operators and external controllers can report Node lifecycle state consistently.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Advancing Workload-Aware Scheduling
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 advances Workload-Aware Scheduling: Workload and PodGroup APIs, gang scheduling, workload-aware preemption, and shared DRA ResourceClaims graduate to Beta. It also introduces Alpha support for CompositePodGroup and multi-level topology-aware scheduling, plus new controller integration APIs and Job controller integration for explicit WAS configuration.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: KubeletInUserNamespace (aka Rootless mode) Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 moves KubeletInUserNamespace to beta and enables the feature gate by default. It allows node components to run as a non-root user in a Linux user namespace, reducing host impact from node-component exploits, while leaving existing rootful clusters unchanged unless explicitly configured.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: DRA Updates
item.description:
Kubernetes 1.37 adds several DRA updates, including GA support for extended resources, stable device taints/tolerations, and stable standardized NUMA node attributes. It also promotes multiple DRA features to Beta or Alpha, with focus areas including workload-level ResourceClaims, device metadata/status, scheduling performance, and fractional consumable capacity.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Scale Workloads to Zero with HorizontalPodAutoscaler
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale workloads down to zero replicas by default when using object or external metrics. The feature is Beta; it requires a metric source that remains available at zero replicas, and the controller marks zero-state ownership with a ScaledToZero condition.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: etcd RangeStream Cuts Memory Use on Large List Reads
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 graduates the EtcdRangeStream feature to beta and enables it by default. With etcd v3.7+, the API server can stream large collection reads instead of assembling whole pages in memory, reducing peak memory use and making it more predictable.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Storage Version Migration Enabled by Default
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes built-in StorageVersionMigration (storagemigration.k8s.io/v1) GA and enabled by default in all clusters. It lets administrators and CRD authors declaratively rewrite stored objects to the current storage version, replacing manual re-write scripts or the out-of-tree migrator.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles
item.description:
Kubernetes 1.37 graduates Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles to GA, adding built-in support for workload X.509 identity and trust bundle distribution. The feature uses Kubelet, PodCertificateRequest objects, and signer controllers to issue and rotate certificates for TLS/mTLS while keeping key material on the node filesystem.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog
